part2.intro: Three young people write about moving to a different country.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Kenji
texts.text: When I first arrived in London from Japan, I was really unhappy. I couldn't speak English well and I didn't understand my classmates' jokes. But my teacher was very kind and gave me extra lessons after school. Now, two years later, I'm one of the best students in my English class! I still miss Japanese food, so my mum and I cook it together at weekends.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Laura
texts.text: My dad got a job in Hanoi, so we moved here from Spain last year. The city is very busy and noisy, which felt strange at first because I'm from a small, quiet village. I love the street food – it's cheap and delicious. I've made friends from lots of different countries at my international school. My best friend is from Korea, and she's teaching me her language.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Amir
texts.text: Moving from Egypt to Canada was exciting, but the winters are terrible! In January it's sometimes minus twenty degrees. I'd never seen snow before, and the first time I saw it I ran outside in my T-shirt! Now I play ice hockey for the school team. I'm not very good yet, but the other players are friendly and help me. I'm lucky to have them.

items.q: Who found it hard to understand people at first?
Who is learning another language from a friend?
Who is in a sports team?
Who sometimes makes food from their home country?
Who comes from a place that is quieter than their new home?
Who was surprised by the weather in their new country?
Who is now very good at a school subject?

part3.title: The young chef who won on TV
part3.text:
Fourteen-year-old Daniel Okoro started cooking when he was nine. 'My mum was very busy at work, and I was always hungry when I got home from school,' he says. 'So I started making simple things like eggs and pasta.' At first his food wasn't very good. 'Once I made a cake that was as hard as a rock!' he laughs.

Last year his cousin saw an advertisement for a TV cooking competition for young people and told Daniel to enter. 'I wasn't sure,' says Daniel. 'I thought the other cooks would be much better than me.' But his mum helped him to fill in the form, and three weeks later he got a phone call – he was in the competition!

The competition was filmed in a big, modern kitchen in London. Each week, the young cooks had to make a different meal in one hour. 'The hardest week was when we had to cook fish,' Daniel remembers. 'I'd never cooked it before, and I was so nervous that I dropped it on the floor!' But the judges liked his sweet potato soup, so he could stay in the competition.

In the final, Daniel cooked a dish from Nigeria, where his grandparents come from. He won! Now he is writing a cookbook for teenagers. 'I want young people to know that cooking isn't difficult,' he says. 'And if you make mistakes, that's fine – I've made hundreds!'

items.q: Why did Daniel start cooking?
options: His mother asked him to cook for the family.
He wanted something to eat after school.
He wanted to learn to make cakes.

items.q: How did Daniel feel when he heard about the competition?
options: He didn't think he was good enough.
He was excited about being on TV.
He was angry with his cousin.

items.q: What happened in the week when the cooks made fish?
options: The judges didn't like Daniel's fish.
Daniel cooked the best fish of all.

items.q: What did Daniel make in the final?
What does Daniel want to tell young people?
options: Cooking is easier than they think.
They should try not to make mistakes.

part4.title: Can pets make us happier?
part4.text:
Millions of people around the world have a pet, and most of them say their animal makes them happy. Scientists now think they are {19}. When people play with a dog or a cat, they often feel calmer and less worried. This is good news for old people who live alone and sometimes feel sad.

Pets are good for children, too. Children who have a pet must {20} after it every day – give it food and water and keep it clean. This helps them to {21} kind and careful.

Dog owners are often healthier because they {22} their dogs for walks every day. And pets can help us make new friends: people often {23} to strangers when they are in the park with their dogs.

But remember – cats and dogs can live for a long {24}, so before you get one, make sure your family has enough time and money to look after it.

part7.instruction: Look at the three pictures. Write the story shown in the pictures. Write 35 words or more.

pictures.caption: a boy in a kitchen reading a recipe to make a birthday cake for his mum
the boy takes a black, burnt cake out of the oven and looks upset
the mother laughing and hugging the boy; they eat strawberries and ice cream

part7.model: It was Mum's birthday, so Ben decided to make her a special cake. He found a recipe and started cooking. But he forgot about the cake while he was watching TV, and when he opened the oven, it was black! Ben felt terrible. But Mum just laughed and gave him a hug, and they ate strawberries and ice cream instead.

items.q: What was the best part of the boy's holiday?

script.t: Did you enjoy your holiday in Italy, Marco?
It was great. The beaches were beautiful, but it was too hot to stay there for long.
Did you go to the theme park?
Yes, but we waited in terrible queues all day. The best part was the boat trip. We saw dolphins!

items.q: How does the girl feel?

script.t: Are you ready for your exam tomorrow, Bella? You look afraid.
Afraid? No, I'm fine – I've studied a lot. I'm just bored because I've read the same book all day.
Aren't you excited about the holidays after the exams?
Not yet! I need a break first. Shall we go for a walk?

items.q: What does the boy's sister look like?

script.t: Is your sister coming to the party, Ben? I've never met her.
Yes, she'll be there. She's tall, with long fair hair.
Does she wear glasses like you?
No, she doesn't. She had short curly hair last year, but it's long now.

items.q: Which animal is the boy afraid of?

script.t: Do you want to come to the zoo with us, Sam? They've got a new snake house.
Sure. I'm not afraid of snakes – I think they're cool.
Really? What about spiders? There are some big ones there.
They're fine too. Actually, it's dogs I don't like. A big dog bit me when I was small.

items.q: What will the friends do this afternoon?

script.t: I'm bored. What shall we do this afternoon? Shall we go swimming?
The pool's closed on Mondays.
Bowling, then?
It's too expensive. Let's play the new video game at my house. My brother says it's brilliant.
OK, great.

part2.intro: You will hear a woman on the radio talking about a writing competition.
part2.title: 'My Amazing Day' Writing Competition

items.label: Winners read their stories on the radio on:

script.t: Hello and welcome to Young Voices. This month we're starting a new writing competition called My Amazing Day. We want you to write about a special day in your life – maybe a day when you were very happy, very lucky, or even very afraid! The competition is for students aged eleven to fifteen. Last year it was only for students over twelve, but this year younger students can enter too. Your story must not be more than three hundred words. Please don't write more, because the judges won't read long stories! Now, the prizes. Last year the winner got a camera, but this year the first prize is a tablet, and there are books for the next five stories. The three best writers will come to our studio and read their stories on the radio. That will be on Thursday next month – not Tuesday, which is the day of our normal programme. Please send your stories to Mrs Penrose. That's P-E-N-R-O-S-E. Good luck, everyone!

part3.intro: You will hear Max talking to his friend Lucy about meeting a famous singer.

items.q: Where did Max meet Jamie Blue?
Who started the conversation with Jamie Blue?
What does Max say about Jamie Blue?
options: He is taller than on TV.
He is quieter than in his videos.

items.q: Why didn't Max get a photo?
options: Jamie Blue didn't want a photo.

items.q: What is Max going to do with his notebook?

script.t: Hi Max. Why are you smiling so much?
You won't believe it, Lucy. Yesterday I met Jamie Blue!
The famous singer? No way! Where? At his concert?
No, I couldn't get tickets for that – they were too expensive. I was in a cafe near the railway station with my mum, and he walked in and sat at the next table!
Lucky you! What did you do?
At first I was too nervous to say anything. My hands were shaking. Mum said, 'Go on, talk to him!' But I couldn't.
So what happened?
He spoke to me first! He saw my T-shirt with his name on it and laughed. He said, 'Nice T-shirt!'
That's so funny! What was he like?
Really friendly. Much shorter than on TV, though. And he was quiet – not loud like in his videos.
Did you get a photo with him?
He was happy to do one, and there was nobody else in the cafe, but my phone battery was dead! And Mum's phone was at home. So he wrote his name in my school notebook instead.
That's still great. Are you going to take it to school and show everyone?
I'll show them a photo of it, but the notebook is staying in a safe place at home. I'm not going to use it for homework any more!
Ha! Good idea.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about a school trip to a museum.
items.q: What did she think of the trip?
options: It was more interesting than she expected.

script.t: I thought the science museum would be boring – my brother said it was. But it was really interesting! There were lots of things you could touch and try. We were there for five hours, but it felt like one. I want to go back with my family soon.

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a new student.
items.q: What does the boy think about the new student?

script.t: What do you think of Nadia, the new girl?
Some people say she's unfriendly because she doesn't talk much. But I think she's just quiet.
She's good at maths, isn't she?
She's brilliant! She answered every difficult question in class today. I'm sure she'll be top of the class.

items.intro: You will hear a boy leaving a message for his friend.
items.q: Why is he calling?
options: to ask his friend to play tennis
to change the time of a dinner

script.t: Hi Leo, it's Danny. I'm really sorry about yesterday. I forgot about our tennis game, and you waited for me in the rain for an hour. I feel terrible. It was a bad thing to do, and I won't do it again. Please call me back – I hope you're not still angry.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her father about the school orchestra.
items.q: How does she feel?

script.t: I'm so tired, Dad. We practised for three hours today!
Oh dear. Do you still want to be in the orchestra?
Of course! The music is so beautiful, and everyone's really friendly. I'm not even worried about the concert any more.
That's great.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking about his grandfather.
items.q: What is special about his grandfather?
options: He has visited lots of countries.

script.t: My grandad is seventy-eight, but he still goes on holiday to a new country every year. He's been to more than forty countries! People think he was rich or famous, but he was a bus driver. He just saved his money carefully. He only speaks English, but he says a smile works everywhere.

part5.intro: You will hear Hoa talking to her friend Ben about her family. What is each person afraid of?

script.t: Hoa, our English homework is about being afraid. Can I ask you about your family?
Sure. Let's start with my dad. He's big and strong, but he's afraid of flying! When we go on holiday, we always go by train.
Really? I thought he didn't like dogs.
No, he loves dogs – we've got two. My mum loves them too. What she really hates is insects. Even a small one in the kitchen makes her scream!
Ha! And your brother Minh?
He says he isn't afraid of anything. But he never swims in the sea now. Last summer he went too far out and couldn't swim back easily. Now he's afraid of deep water.
Poor Minh. What about your grandma?
Grandma's amazing. She climbs mountains, so she isn't afraid of high places at all. But she hates storms. When there's thunder, she hides under a blanket!
And you, Hoa?
Me? I was afraid of the dark when I was little, but not now. Now it's snakes. I saw one in our garden once – it was terrible!
Thanks, Hoa. That's really useful.
